For students planning to apply for the 2027 May intake, understanding university timelines, available courses, entry requirements, and application processes is essential. Course availability, tuition fees, scholarships, English requirements, and academic documentation all play an important role in preparing a successful application.

Choosing a university is only one part of the process. Researching the right course, understanding university requirements, and preparing your application documents properly can help you make informed decisions.

If you are still building your overall study plan, it can help to understand what studying in the UK involves for an international student before narrowing your university choices.

This guide covers the key information you need for May 2027.

For the 2027 cycle, the UCAS application fee is £34.50. One payment allows an undergraduate applicant to add up to five university or college choices.

Postgraduate admissions work differently. There is no single national master's deadline. Universities normally accept postgraduate applications directly, with dates varying by course.

Here is the thing: an application portal can still be open when the best time to apply has already passed. Popular courses, scholarships and accommodation can become limited well before the final closing date.

September Intake Universities in UK 2027

The September intake is the main entry period across UK higher education. Universities may describe their courses as September entry, autumn entry or simply 2027 entry.

Students outside the UK sometimes search for the fall intake in UK, but British universities usually use "autumn" rather than "fall".

Some institutions begin teaching in early October rather than September. They still belong to the same main autumn admissions cycle.

The University of Manchester already lists courses for September 2027, while the University of Birmingham has published its 2027/28 academic calendar.

Oxford also confirms its 15 October 2026 application deadline for 2027 undergraduate entry.

Do not choose from this list purely by university reputation.

Start with your subject. Then compare entry requirements, tuition fees, professional accreditation, placements, scholarship opportunities, city costs and the exact 2027 start date.

That produces a much stronger shortlist.

"Affordable" is relative. A university with a £17,000 tuition fee in a lower-cost city could leave you with a smaller overall budget than a slightly cheaper course in London.

Many institutions have not yet confirmed their international tuition fees for 2027/28. For that reason, the figures below use the latest official published international fees as planning benchmarks, not guaranteed 2027 prices.

The University of Chester, for example, currently lists a standard international undergraduate fee of about £14,950, and some course pages already show September 2027 as a start option.

Teesside currently publishes a standard international undergraduate fee of £17,000, while Hertfordshire lists £17,450 for standard undergraduate study.

These figures can change for 2027 entry, so use them to build an initial budget rather than treating them as final quotations.

You can also compare other UK universities where international tuition may be more manageable before deciding where to apply.

Undergraduate September Intake Options in UK

September offers the widest range of undergraduate courses because it follows the main UCAS admissions cycle.

Popular options include:

  • Business and Management
  • Computer Science
  • Accounting and Finance
  • Engineering
  • Law
  • Psychology
  • Architecture
  • Economics
  • Media and Communications
  • International Relations
  • Health-related subjects

Do not choose a degree simply because it appears on a popular-course list.

Suppose you want to work in technology. Computer Science may suit one student, while Cyber Security, Software Engineering or Artificial Intelligence could be a better fit for another. Entry requirements and course content matter more than the broad subject name.

If you are still comparing subjects, look at different UK degree options against your background and career goals before committing to a university.

Undergraduate applicants should also understand how their choices, reference and application move through UCAS. You can work through that application process before submitting.

There is no universal postgraduate September deadline.

For many international applicants, October 2026 to March 2027 is a useful working period for submitting applications, but this is planning guidance rather than a national deadline.

Competitive programmes may become full earlier. Other courses continue accepting applications much later.

A course being open and a course still offering its best opportunity are not always the same thing.

Best Courses in UK With September Intake

Business and Management, Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Public Health, Law, Cyber Security and Project Management are among the subjects commonly available during the main intake.

The stronger approach is to compare related courses rather than choosing from a generic popularity list.

For example, a student interested in analytics might compare:

Business Analytics if they want to connect data with commercial decisions.

Data Science if they prefer statistics, programming and technical modelling.

Artificial Intelligence if they want deeper exposure to machine learning and intelligent systems.

That level of comparison helps you choose the course first, then identify universities that fit it.

Deadline for September Intake in UK 2027

For most undergraduate courses, the key UCAS deadline is 13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time.

This is the equal-consideration deadline. Applications received by then should receive equal consideration from universities and colleges.

An earlier deadline of 15 October 2026 applies to Oxford, Cambridge and most undergraduate courses in medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine or science.

Applications can still be possible later where vacancies remain.

UCAS Extra opens on 25 February 2027 for eligible applicants who have used their choices and are not holding an offer. Applications submitted after the main late-June point move into Clearing.

The final UCAS application date sits much later in September 2027, but students should not use that as their normal target.

The later you leave it, the fewer suitable courses may remain.

For postgraduate study, universities set their own deadlines. Some use fixed dates. Others use rolling admissions.

Treat a deadline as the final boundary, not the date you should aim to submit.

In real applications, the form itself is rarely the only time-consuming part.

References may take time. Academic transcripts may need updates. English language results and university documentation require careful planning.

Build spare time into the process rather than planning every stage around the latest possible date.

May Intake Universities in UK Fees and Cost

The intake does not determine your tuition fee. Your university, course, study level and location do.

Current British Council guidance gives a broad international undergraduate tuition range of around £11,400-£38,000 per year and a postgraduate range of roughly £9,000-£30,000.

Your overall study budget depends on your university, accommodation type, location and personal spending habits.

These figures are general planning estimates and should be used as a guide when comparing UK universities and courses.

Location can change your total budget dramatically.

A £17,000 course outside London can sometimes cost less overall than a £15,500 course in London once accommodation and everyday expenses are included.

Scholarships for September Intake in the UK

Applications for 2027/28 Chevening Scholarships opened on 4 August 2026 and close on 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC.

Chevening is a fully funded UK Government scholarship for eligible master's applicants. Students should check the official Chevening application timeline rather than waiting for their university deadline.

The current GREAT Scholarships programme offers £10,000 towards tuition fees for eligible students taking selected one-year taught postgraduate programmes. The participating countries, universities and courses can change by academic year, so check the relevant 2027/28 programme once it is published.

Universities may also offer:

  • merit scholarships;
  • country-specific awards;
  • subject scholarships;
  • tuition discounts;
  • early-payment discounts.

That is why you should research UK scholarship options while shortlisting universities, not after receiving your final offer.

Entry Requirements for September 2027

There is no single academic requirement across UK universities.

Undergraduate applicants normally need recognised secondary qualifications, suitable subject grades and English-language evidence. Competitive courses may also require admissions tests, interviews, written work or portfolios.

Postgraduate applicants generally need a recognised bachelor's degree. Depending on the programme, universities may also ask for work experience, a CV, references, a statement of purpose or portfolio.

English-language requirements

IELTS is widely accepted, alongside PTE Academic, TOEFL and other evidence approved by individual institutions.

As a general planning range:

Level

Common IELTS Planning Range

Undergraduate

Around 6.0-6.5

Postgraduate

Around 6.5-7.0

These are not universal entry requirements.

Some courses require higher overall scores or specific minimum marks in reading, writing, listening and speaking.

Check the individual course before booking a test. You can also compare the English requirements commonly used by UK universities.

Some applicants may meet the language condition through an alternative accepted route. If that might apply to you, check possible ways of meeting university English requirements without IELTS.

Documents Required for September Intake Applications

Prepare the core documents before the busy deadline period.

Undergraduate applicants commonly need:

  • academic qualifications or predicted grades;
  • passport details;
  • an academic reference;
  • the required UCAS application information;
  • English-language evidence where applicable.

Postgraduate applicants may need:

  • degree certificate;
  • academic transcripts;
  • passport;
  • CV;
  • statement of purpose or personal statement;
  • academic or professional references;
  • English-language evidence;
  • portfolio or work-experience documents for relevant courses.

One practical issue deserves more attention than it normally gets.

Plan the academic and financial sides of the application together.

How to Apply for May Intake in UK

1. Choose the course first

Identify the subject and programme that match your academic background, career goals and future plans. Researching available study options can help you understand which course pathway is most suitable before selecting a university.

2. Check the official 2027 course page

Confirm the May intake availability, entry requirements, tuition fees and application deadlines directly from the university course page.

Do not rely only on a general university information page. Always check the specific programme details and requirements.

3. Build a balanced shortlist

Consider different university options that match your academic profile and long-term goals.

4. Submit through the correct route

Most undergraduate students apply through UCAS, while postgraduate students usually apply directly to universities.

For undergraduate applicants, understanding the application process and required documents early can help avoid delays.

For the 2027 undergraduate cycle, the UCAS application fee is £34.50 and covers up to five choices.

5. Respond to your offer

Complete academic, English-language or document requirements within the university’s stated timeline.

If the university requires a tuition deposit, make sure you understand the payment schedule and university terms before proceeding.

6. Complete your enrolment preparation

After meeting the university’s conditions, follow the institution’s enrolment process and prepare for your studies in the UK.

International students can explore UK study guidance for international students and review available university support options before starting their academic journey.

UK Study Preparation for September Intake

International students planning to study an eligible UK course should understand the university requirements and preparation steps before starting their academic journey.

After receiving an offer and completing the required academic conditions, students should follow the university’s enrolment process and prepare the necessary documentation for joining their chosen institution.

Students may need to prepare:

  • a valid passport or identification document;
  • university offer and enrolment documents;
  • academic certificates and transcripts;
  • English-language evidence where applicable;
  • additional documents required by the university or course.

Requirements can vary depending on the university, course and individual circumstances. Students should always check the latest information from their chosen university and relevant official sources before making decisions.

Careful planning of academic documents, university requirements and enrolment steps can help students prepare for a smoother transition into UK higher education.

September Intake Start Date in UK

There is no single September intake start date across the UK.

Most universities hold registration, induction or Welcome Week during September, with teaching beginning from mid-September to early October.

For a concrete 2027 example, the University of Birmingham's academic calendar lists 20-24 September 2027 for Welcome Week and 27 September 2027 for the start of its autumn term.

Manchester is already listing undergraduate programmes specifically for September 2027.

Before booking travel, check four dates:

  • accommodation move-in;
  • registration or enrolment;
  • course start date;
  • latest permitted arrival.

Your university's official course information and offer documents should be treated as the final authority.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which universities offer September intake in the UK for 2027?

Many universities recruit through the main autumn cycle, including Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds, Sheffield, Southampton, Nottingham, Warwick, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Newcastle, Cardiff, Queen Mary, Hertfordshire, Portsmouth, Northumbria and Chester.

Oxford and Cambridge also belong to the main annual admissions cycle, although their academic terms normally begin in October.

When should I apply for September intake in UK 2027?

Undergraduate applications can be submitted through UCAS from 1 September 2026. Most undergraduate courses use 13 January 2027 as their equal-consideration deadline.

What is the last date to apply for September intake in UK?

There is no single ideal last date for every applicant.

For undergraduate study, UCAS continues accepting applications beyond the main January deadline, but later applications depend increasingly on vacancies.

Postgraduate closing dates are set by individual universities.

What are the best courses in UK with September intake?

Popular choices include Business and Management, Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Engineering, Finance, Accounting, Cyber Security, Public Health, Law and Project Management.

The best programme for you depends on your previous studies, career plans and entry profile.

Which are affordable UK universities with September intake?

Universities such as Chester, Teesside, Hertfordshire and Portsmouth currently publish international tuition figures towards the lower end of the broader UK fee range for many standard programmes.

Always compare the exact course fee and living costs before deciding which option is genuinely cheaper.

How much does September intake in UK cost?

Current international tuition fees vary widely depending on the university, course and study level. British Council guidance places undergraduate study at around £11,400-£38,000 per year and postgraduate study at roughly £9,000-£30,000.

Students should also consider additional study costs such as accommodation, travel, daily living expenses and other university-related expenses when planning their overall budget.

What is the UCAS application fee for 2027 entry?

The UCAS undergraduate application fee for the 2027 cycle is £34.50. The single payment covers up to five university or college choices.

Can I apply for September intake without IELTS?

Possibly.

Some universities accept PTE, TOEFL or other recognised English tests. In eligible circumstances, a university may also accept alternative evidence of English proficiency.

The exact policy depends on the course and institution.

Is September the main intake for UK universities?

Yes. September or autumn entry is the main admissions cycle for most UK universities and generally offers the widest range of undergraduate and postgraduate courses.

Planning Your September 2027 UK Application

The September intake universities in UK offer more course choices and opportunities than other main admission periods, but having more options only helps when you compare them carefully.

A structured approach keeps every part of your application moving together and gives you more time to make informed decisions before deadlines become urgent.
